items.title: From Kerala’s fishing villages to CBD COP17: The fight to recognise traditional knowledge
items.summary: Twelve-year-old Gabriel’s painting depicts two men at sea, practising kanicham , a traditional method of visual triangulation used by artisanal fishers along the coast of Kerala’s Thiruvananthapuram to navigate and locate fishing grounds. Nearby, 10-year-old Joe’s artwork captures women carrying their catch, while 13-year-old Lena takes viewers beneath the waves, bringing the biodiversity of the underwater world to life. The paintings, along with several others portraying the lives, livelihoods and knowledge of south Kerala’s coastal communities, found a place in two pavilions at the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), which began in Yerevan, Armenia, on October 19. The children themselves were not present at the conference, but their work drew appreciation from delegates from across the world. Beyond their colours and detail, the paintings carried a larger message from the fishing communities of Thiruvananthapuram: their knowledge of the sea, passed down through generations, is an essential part of conserving marine biodiversity, yet it remains insufficiently recognised in scientific research and global conservatio
